notes:
v2.8.0 lets you charge a job's materials the same way as logged time, holds customer overpayments as credit in Bank Rec, and fixes bank rules for OFX statements.

Materials charged like logged time: a job's purchase order can now be marked Charge to customer, with a markup (15% unless you change it; it's on by default for a new PO on a job). Its materials then go on the job's next invoice as lines at cost plus markup, without a separate invoice. They're added when you invoice completed tasks, ticked in the claim builder, and offered under Materials to charge when you add tasks or materials to an invoice. The job's Purchasing tab shows which POs are still to invoice and which invoice each went on. A PO can't be charged twice, and voiding the invoice frees it to charge again.

Customer paid more than they owe: in Bank Rec, a deposit bigger than the customer's invoices can now be recorded. Tick their invoices, then tick Hold $X as credit for the customer. The invoices are marked paid and the rest stays on the customer's account as credit, ready to use on their next invoice with More > Apply Credit. Before, the statement line couldn't be reconciled.

Bank rules work with OFX statements: a rule now matches its text in either the description or the reference. Some banks put the text in a different field in their OFX download than in their CSV, so rules saved from CSV lines stopped matching after switching to OFX. The Match Field choice has been removed from the rule form because it's no longer needed.

The Bank Reconciliation and Invoices guides under Help cover the new credit option.
